source.title: SozKZ: Training Efficient Small Language Models for Kazakh from Scratch

record.file_problem: The full paper is present, with minor encoding/OCR artifacts in some headings and figure labels. Table 2 omits the SozKZ-50M MC QA value, but the text reports it as 22.8%.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests downstream performance across model sizes in Kazakh, a low-resource language setting, rather than testing the original held-out cross-entropy scaling measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper reports downstream benchmark accuracy for four SozKZ sizes and describes a scaling analysis. It does not report held-out pretraining cross-entropy, compute-optimal parameter/token allocations, or a test of shape sensitivity. The plotted power-law fit is for average benchmark accuracy, not pretraining loss. Multilingual models are reported as benchmark comparators, not as a controlled scaling sweep.
record.test_reason: The study trains four Kazakh-only Llama-style models (50M–600M) on the same 9B tokens and reports zero-shot downstream accuracy at each size, plus a power-law fit of average accuracy versus parameters. That bears on V6 (downstream gains with scale) in a new low-resource language setting. It reports no pretraining loss, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that MC QA rises consistently from 22.8% to 30.3% with no sign of saturation, so further scaling should help. They describe SIB-200 as stable across sizes, attributing this to the tokenizer, and Belebele as improving modestly. Their main conclusion, though, is that small dedicated Kazakh models are competitive with 2–5× larger multilingual models. The paraphrase should mention that.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains Kazakh-only models from scratch and measures downstream benchmark accuracy over four sizes; it does not reproduce the original loss-versus-parameters/tokens/compute experiments or compute-optimal allocation analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: Benchmark changes the observed size trend: MC QA improves, Belebele changes modestly and non-monotonically, and SIB-200 is flat.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. The size sweep has four SozKZ models, and downstream benchmark accuracy is not the held-out pretraining loss used by the scaling-law claims. The paper's scaling plot fits average benchmark accuracy rather than cross-entropy loss.
record.rows_left_out: The five multilingual competitors' benchmark scores in Table 2 are omitted because the paper presents them as cross-family comparators, not as a controlled scaling sweep; their sizes, training data, and model families differ.

untested.parts: Predictability of downstream performance from pretraining loss (no loss reported). Extrapolation of downstream accuracy to larger runs. Scaling beyond 600M or across other model families. In this sweep tokens are fixed at 9B and only parameters (and compute with them) vary.

missing.what: Power-law fit of average benchmark accuracy versus parameters, y = 23.59·x^0.023. The exponent is very small and no fit quality is reported. This is the paper's only explicit scaling fit.

record.verdict_notes: Several confounds weaken the scaling test. All sizes see the same 9B tokens, so data is not scaled. The 150M model uses a 1,024 context versus 2,048 for the others. Peak learning rates differ, and depth and width vary together. There are only four points and no uncertainty estimates. The identical 25.5% SIB-200 score at every size may indicate degenerate predictions, for example a constant class; the paper does not check this. MC QA at 50M and 150M is below chance. The 50M MC QA value appears only in the text, not in Table 2. The omitted multilingual comparators are rightly excluded: they are not a controlled sweep.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss curves against parameters, tokens, or compute.
No extrapolation from smaller-run loss fits to larger runs.
No fixed-compute comparison or estimate of compute-optimal parameter and token counts.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
The study uses text pretraining and does not test other modalities or the listed alternative training regimes.
Tests downstream benchmark accuracy across four SozKZ parameter sizes, but not whether downstream performance is predictable from pretraining loss or across other model families and training setups.
No comparison of fitting methods, parameter-counting choices, schedules, or data setups for loss exponents or compute-optimal allocations.
